_about: Anatomical centring landmarks for the x-ray protocols, measured by tools/measure_landmarks.py. Volume-frame entries are cm from the volume centre (x, y, z; +z superior) and are mapped to the world through the same flips and rotation as the phantom. Entries marked frame:"world" are already in the x-ray world frame. Re-run the tool after rebuilding a model.

knee.how: joint-space valley between the condyles and the plateau (prominence 15.3 cm2)

ankle.how: peak of the malleolar bulge — the clinical centring point, midway between the malleoli; tibia and talus are fused in the segmentation, so there is no joint-space dip to find

hip.how: peak of the proximal bulge: femoral head and trochanters

femur.how: midway between the knee and hip landmarks

foot.how: tarsals, 5 cm above the inferior end — the foot points anteriorly in this supine leg

elbow.how: widest mediolateral span of the distal humerus within 8 cm above the forearm (which ends at 31.8 cm): the epicondyles

forearm.how: middle of the two-bone (radius + ulna) zone

wrist.how: 1.5 cm distal of where the two forearm bones begin: the carpals

shoulder.how: peak of the proximal bulge: humeral head

humerus.how: midway between the elbow and shoulder landmarks

wrist.how: 2 cm proximal of the first slice that cuts all five metacarpals: the carpals

hand.how: distal end of the five-metacarpal zone: the MCP joints, the PA hand centring point

fingers.how: midway from the MCP joints to the fingertips: PIP level

skull.how: bone-weighted centre of the upper half (the cranium)

cspine.how: C4 vertebral body, from the CT's own vertebra labels (s1397), registered to the model (99.8% of label voxels on bone)

kub.how: iliac crest (= L4/L5), from the DXA landmark finder

abdomenErect.how: 5 cm above the crest, to include the diaphragm

pelvis.how: midway between the ASIS (-20.0 / -15.8, mean -17.9) and the pubic symphysis (-29.4)

lumbar.how: L3: crest (L4/L5) + 1.5 x the measured 3.6 cm lumbar period; AP depth = centre of the vertebral body

thoracic.how: T7: L1 + six thoracic bodies at ~2.6 cm (estimated, not measured); AP depth = centre of the vertebral body

femoralHeadL.how: centre of the 2.2 cm sphere through the most cortical bone (head and acetabular shells)

femoralHeadR.how: centre of the 2.2 cm sphere through the most cortical bone (head and acetabular shells)
